findings.title: Audience enters the disclosure field
findings.claim: The addressed audience moves from being told to know into the field of acts it actively discloses before Allah.
findings.mechanism: The second-person plural Form IV verb carries the audience as agent, while the supplied boundary relation connects that audience to the open disclosure object under divine knowledge.
findings.reader_payoff: The audience is present inside the accountability statement rather than standing outside it as a merely addressed group.
findings.containment: This keeps the local audience and disclosure relation; it does not infer an unprovided motive or result for what they disclose.

epistemic.reason: The focus morphology and candidate-specific boundary support directly establish the audience chain.

findings.title: Disclosure has an agent
findings.claim: The disclosure verb presents the audience as actively bringing something into view.
findings.mechanism: Its active Form IV shape assigns causative disclosure to the second-person plural subject, and the supplied contrast preserves that agency against passive manifestation.
findings.reader_payoff: What becomes visible is heard as something the audience makes public, not merely something that happens to be seen.
findings.containment: The contrast is local to verbal voice and agency; it does not deny that disclosure can have a visible result.

epistemic.reason: The focus form and candidate-specific contrast are both trusted and directly aligned.

findings.title: One audience carries both poles
findings.claim: The disclosure and concealment verbs bind their opposite actions to the same plural audience.
findings.mechanism: The shared second-person plural endings repeat the same addressed subject across the two verbs, so the visible and hidden poles remain paired actions of one group.
findings.reader_payoff: The opposition does not split into two populations; one audience is held across the full range.
findings.containment: The cadence establishes shared address and does not add a claim about uniform behavior within that audience.

epistemic.reason: The candidate-specific support identifies the shared morphology and cadence directly.

findings.title: Disclosure is caused
findings.claim: The local disclosure term describes the audience causing something to appear.
findings.mechanism: The Form IV causative verb assigns an active making-visible operation to the addressed subject, and its open object remains whatever is disclosed.
findings.reader_payoff: Disclosure carries agency and an act of emergence rather than a neutral state of visibility.
findings.containment: The emergence image colors the selected causative disclosure sense; it is not a separate physical scene.

epistemic.reason: QAC form data and the candidate-specific support agree on the active causative relation.

findings.title: Disclosure enters total awareness
findings.claim: The disclosure clause participates in a local total-awareness pattern that holds public and hidden action together.
findings.mechanism: The supplied formula evidence meets the focus pair of disclosure and concealment, so the knowledge predicate reaches both poles rather than only the visible one.
findings.reader_payoff: The statement feels comprehensive at the point where disclosure first appears, even before concealment is completed.
findings.containment: The formula relation supports this focus-local pairing; it does not make a surah-wide thesis or add unnamed objects.

epistemic.reason: The formula support is concrete and the paired object structure is present in the focus.

findings.title: An open field comes into view
findings.claim: Disclosure carries an exposed-open-field coloration while remaining the local active making-visible sense.
findings.mechanism: The appearance image meets the causative disclosure form, giving the act a movement from hiddenness into view without replacing the verb's local selection.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel disclosure as opening a field, not only as reporting a preselected item.
findings.containment: The appearance image is bounded coloration; it is not a separate desert-root reading or a claim that every object is fully exposed.

epistemic.reason: The candidate-specific support explicitly preserves the image as color and narrows the local form.

findings.mechanism: The second-person plural verb is transitive and takes the preceding open relative particle as its object, joining audience agency to an intentionally unspecified content field.
findings.reader_payoff: The disclosure statement remains broad without needing a list of acts.
findings.containment: The open object is retained as open; this does not enumerate content or infer that disclosure means approval.

epistemic.reason: The candidate-specific support states the transitive attachment and the focus alignment supplies the form.

epistemic.reason: The candidate-specific support identifies the coordination and equal object-domain relation.
